## 1. What was read

**1,088 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 538 | 220 | 88 | 222 | 20 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo -26%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 122, JAMA 118, Science 108, J Immunother Cancer 59, Nucleic Acids Res 52, Cell 49.

## 3. The evidence that moved it


**The checkpoint roster this month is TIM-3, PILRalpha/CD99, CLEVER-1, Cbl-b and
CISH, plus IDO1, ENT1, OX40 and LAG-3.** Of these, exactly one — CISH — has a
first-in-human trial, and it works by gene editing rather than blockade. By
August, zero of the five headline names appear anywhere in the corpus. The
half-life measurement that the later briefings quote starts here, and this is
the month it can be checked against a written list rather than a recollection.

**Tumour antigens preferentially derive from unmutated genomic sequences**
([40405018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40405018/), *Nat Cancer*), and
pancreatic cancer-restricted **cryptic** antigens are targets for T cell
recognition ([40339010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40339010/), *Science*).
Two independent statements in one month that the immunogenic target space is not
where the mutation-calling pipeline is looking. The neoantigen thread's later
troubles — prediction models exploiting shortcuts, immunoediting stripping clonal
targets — are downstream of this.

**DYNAMIC reports five-year outcomes**
([40055522](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40055522/)): ctDNA-guided adjuvant
therapy in stage II colon cancer, randomized, mature. This is the thread's
strongest support in the corpus, and it is worth naming because almost everything
that lands on `ctdna-mrd` afterwards is a refutation. The distinction that
survives: ctDNA works as a **de-escalation** trigger, and has repeatedly failed as
an **escalation** trigger.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[39918337](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39918337/) (*Cancer Discov*): stromal
KITL maintains pancreas homeostasis and *restrains* tumour progression, with a
companion arguing that stellate cells uphold inherent microenvironmental tumour
suppression. Pancreatic stroma depletion has been a therapeutic goal for a
decade.

[40316306](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40316306/): FMO2-positive
cancer-associated fibroblasts *sensitize* anti-PD-1 therapy in hepatocellular
carcinoma patients — human data, not mouse.
[40210998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40210998/): Tregs augment self-tolerance
during infection.

### (b) Method credibility

[40346587](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40346587/): most human DNA replication
initiation is dispersed, with only a minority inside previously annotated
initiation zones. The reference annotation captures the minority case.

[40193392](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40193392/): standard negative sampling
leaves an exploitable shortcut in protein-protein interaction prediction. This is
the same finding February 2026 reports for transcription-factor binding sites and
May 2026 for drug synergy — the negative set, not the model, is where the
performance came from. Three instances, ten months apart, in three subfields, and
none of them cites the others.

[40341387](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40341387/): bacterial pan-genome
analysis approaches carry pitfalls that show up as soon as the species is not
clonal.

[40339003](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40339003/) (*Science*): a published
Cambrian mollusc is reassigned to a different phylum-level group. Out of corpus
scope, carded because the audit ledger should include the case where the original
claim was simply wrong about what the object was.
